relevance_rank_note: Direct test of B in astrocytes: surface LRP1 by four methods in ApoE4 vs ApoE3 knock-in mouse astrocytes, with NHE6 and HDAC-inhibitor rescue of surface LRP1; mouse cultured cells, no ARF6, endocytosis rate unchanged so the deficit is placed at recycling/delivery.

description: Surface biotinylation showed plasma-membrane LRP1 about 50% lower in ApoE4 than ApoE3 astrocytes (normalised to Na+/K+ ATPase), with total LRP1 unchanged (see null row).
quote: (B) Surface biotinylation (Left) and quantification (Right) of biological triplicates showing that plasma membrane levels of LRP1 are depressed by ∼50% in ApoE4 astrocytes, relative to ApoE3 (**P = 0.0022, Student’s t test; n = 3).
system: Cultured astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE3 or APOE4 (cells from ref 23, Verghese et al. 2013); endogenous human ApoE expression; cell-surface biotinylation, LRP1 immunoblot normalised to Na+/K+ ATPase, biological triplicates. Mouse astrocytes (human APOE gene only); in vitro cell culture; donor age not stated; possibly an immortalized line.
human_check: Authors print '∼50%'. Main text does not say whether these astrocytes are primary or immortalized; ref 23 (Verghese 2013) should be checked - likely the immortalized APOE-TR astrocyte lines. Class 1 -> 3 (team leader, 2026-11-21): steady-state surface level is B' in the directness guide; synthesis or breakdown could also change it, so it does not measure recycling itself.

system: Cultured astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human APOE3 or APOE4 (ref 23); surface antibody labelling of 10,000 live nonpermeabilised cells, FACS, biological triplicates. Mouse astrocytes with human APOE; in vitro culture; donor age not stated.

quote: Note lower LRP1 staining in ApoE4 astrocytes, relative to ApoE3, due to reduced surface expression.

description: Rescue: ectopic GFP-NHE6 expression in ApoE4 astrocytes raised surface LRP1 immunofluorescence about 2.5-fold vs empty-vector ApoE4 cells (surface biotinylation in SI Fig S7C gave about 5.7-fold, without change in total LRP1), implicating NHE6 loss as the cause of the ApoE4 surface deficit.
quote: Compared with the weak surface LRP1 staining in vector-transfected ApoE4 astrocytes, we observed prominent, ∼2.5-fold higher LRP1 staining in ApoE4 cells expressing ectopic NHE6 (Fig. 4F).
system: ApoE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes (ApoE-KO background, human APOE4; ref 23) transfected with GFP-tagged NHE6 vs empty vector; surface immunofluorescence of nonpermeabilised cells. In vitro; overexpression; contrast is NHE6 vs vector within ApoE4.
human_check: n = 40 cells per condition. Effect is NHE6 vs vector in ApoE4 cells; no ApoE3 arm in this panel.

description: Rescue: the HDAC inhibitor trichostatin A (5 uM, 12 h), which restored NHE6 expression and endosomal pH, roughly doubled surface LRP1 (4 C surface labelling, flow cytometry) in ApoE4 astrocytes vs DMSO.
quote: Importantly, we observed prominent, approximately twofold higher surface LRP1 expression in ApoE4 cells with TSA treatment (Fig. 5E and SI Appendix, Fig. S8G).
summary: (ApoE4 + HDAC inhibitor TSA -> NHE6 up) -> (more surface LRP1)
system: ApoE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes (ref 23) treated with TSA vs DMSO; surface LRP1 labelling at 4 C and flow cytometry, n = 3. Mouse astrocytes with human APOE; in vitro; pharmacological HDAC inhibition with broad off-target effects; no ApoE3 arm.
human_check: Authors print 'approximately twofold'; bar ~200 vs 100. Contrast is TSA vs DMSO within ApoE4.

description: Confocal imaging showed LRP1 lost from astrocyte processes and accumulated perinuclearly in ApoE4 vs ApoE3 cells, and LRP1 colocalised with endocytosed transferrin in ApoE4 astrocytes, consistent with endosomal sequestration of the receptor. No P is given: these are representative images without quantification, and the transferrin image shows APOE4 cells only.
quote: Confocal microscopy revealed a striking loss of LRP1 from astrocyte processes and increased perinuclear accumulation in ApoE4 cells, relative to ApoE3 (Fig. 2F).
system: ApoE3 and ApoE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes (ref 23); LRP1 immunofluorescence (permeabilised), confocal with orthogonal slices; LRP1 + fluorescent transferrin colocalisation. Mouse astrocytes with human APOE; in vitro; donor age not stated.
human_check: Representative images only, no quantification; Fig 2G shows ApoE4 cells only, so the transferrin colocalisation has no ApoE3 comparison.

description: Mechanism: NHE6 protein was about 45% lower in ApoE4 than ApoE3 astrocytes by Western blot (NHE6 transcript about 56% lower in ApoE4 knock-in cells, SI Fig S5E), proposed as the cause of endosomal hyperacidification and the LRP1 recycling block.
quote: (C, Top) Western blot analysis of NHE6 protein revealed that it was ∼45% lower in ApoE4 astrocytes, relative to ApoE3. (C, Bottom) Densitometric quantification of the monomeric and dimeric forms of NHE6 relative to β-actin (***P = 0.0009, Student’s t test; n = 4).
system: ApoE3 and ApoE4 knock-in mouse astrocytes (ref 23); Western blot of NHE6 normalised to beta-actin, n = 4. Mouse astrocytes with human APOE; in vitro.

description: Transferrin uptake (60 min, flow cytometry) was about 1.5-fold HIGHER in ApoE4 than ApoE3 astrocytes (about twofold by confocal, Fig 1E), so the constitutively recycling transferrin receptor pathway is not reduced in ApoE4 cells; the effect is cargo-selective.
